weeks_note: Durations are working weeks from the phase's start: low / likely / high. Dependencies: 'finish' = starts when that phase finishes; 'start' = starts lag_weeks after that phase starts.

phases.name: Domain research and planning
phases.summary: Domain knowledge base, 135 canonical invariants, 500-feature list, Kyle's rulings, tech stack.

phases.name: Schema at parity with the invariants
phases.summary: Close the 80 open invariants in seven waves. Wave 1 landed as v5.4.2-19. Kyle's 2026-10-14 answers unblock tax jurisdictions, franchise fees and the PGA billing side.

parts.name: Wave 1: close holes in what is built
Wave 2: finance structures and cash handling
Tax jurisdictions, tax stack, franchise fees (Kyle answered)

phases.name: Scenarios and testing strategy
phases.summary: Write the 200-390 scenarios the core must pass, have Kyle check the numbers, and choose how they become tests.

parts.name: State machines, exception paths, persona matrix
Worked bills with dollar figures (Kyle checks)

phases.name: Core build plan
phases.summary: Break the C# core into ordered build phases, each with its scenarios as the finish line. Choose the launch feature set.

parts.name: Launch feature set chosen from the 439 required features
Core sub-phases, order and exit tests

phases.name: Platform foundation
phases.summary: AWS environments, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, staff login, the .NET solution, and database access that sets the tenant on every connection.

phases.name: Core billing engine (C#)
phases.summary: The billing engine and API, built in sub-phases planned in P3. Each sub-phase finishes when its scenarios pass.

parts.name: Rate calculation (tariffs, PGA, heating value, WNA, taxes, franchise)

phases.name: Frontend hardening and integration
phases.summary: Take the prototype (36 screens on made-up data) to production: real login, roles, the generated API client, error states, accessibility.

parts.name: Decide: harden the prototype or rebuild from it

phases.name: Integrations
phases.summary: The outside systems a utility cannot run without. Vendors depend on the first customer's contracts.

phases.name: Test data and release testing
phases.summary: A synthetic utility with a year of history, end-to-end tests, and a full billing-run load test. The fixtures are built from P2 onward; this phase is the final pass.

parts.name: Synthetic utility (meters, accounts, 13 months of reads)
Scenario suite green end to end

phases.name: Security and operations readiness
phases.summary: Backups and disaster recovery, monitoring, an outside penetration test, incident runbooks, and SOC 2 groundwork.

phases.name: First customer: conversion and setup
phases.summary: Needs a signed customer. Convert their data from the old system, load their tariffs and ordinances, and train their staff.

parts.name: Data conversion from the old billing system

phases.name: Parallel billing runs
phases.summary: Bill the customer's real cycles on both systems and reconcile every difference. 2 to 4 monthly cycles.

phases.name: Go-live and stabilization
phases.summary: Cut over, then close support for the first live billing cycles.

parts.name: First live cycle billed and paid
